reason: The one launcher is kept as cmd/dsh plus internal/cli: two-stage parsing, profile launch, bounded shutdown and a start-up failure report all survive. Changed: launcher options come before the command or profile name, the three dump switches and profile creation become fixed commands, dsh plugin manages local directories instead of forwarding to pnpm, shutdown goes through one stop function that ends the turn in the log before a configurable deadline, and every command shares one output contract and one closed exit-status table. The package's 91 workspace dependencies are a composition list that the boot and bundle areas own.

The launcher stays the root of the command tree. Changed: options (--home, --profile, --layer, --safe) are written before the command or profile name instead of ending at the first unknown word; --patch is renamed --layer; --dump-config, --dump-default-config and --dump-config-schema become dsh config show, dsh config show --defaults and dsh config schema; --from-default-profile becomes dsh profile new and dsh profile reset; -V and help are kept.

dsh web is kept as the one launch command: it starts the host, prints the launch URL as the only line on standard output and opens the system browser. All seven upstream options survive (--host is renamed --bind to match the host area) and --insecure-remote is added. New behaviour: a second dsh web for the same home and address reuses the running host, and one with listener-changing flags is refused.

dsh headless is kept: one task, the final assistant text on standard output, diagnostics on standard error, exit 0 only for a completed turn, --json for one event per line, --permission-mode, --approval-policy and --add-dir unchanged. Changed: --session-id is renamed --session, --command runs one human command, the JSON lines use the session export line format, approvals are asked on a controlling terminal through the cli answerer or refused when there is none, and Ctrl-C closes the turn in the log before exit 130.

dsh sdk is kept with no options: standard output carries only protocol frames and the process ends on end of input, shutdown or a signal. The command-line area fixes the launch form programs use (dsh --home <dir> --profile sdk) and the three exit statuses the SDK area asked for: 0 clean, 125 stalled client, 124 forced.

Upstream ships a fifth profile that serves the same SDK protocol over a standalone minimal tree. The Go design keeps it as the built-in profile sdk-minimal, which area A27 defines as the bundles core, minimal and sdk (DH-ADR-BUNDLE-2) and which the launcher starts by name under rule 2 of the grammar like every other profile; there is no bundle of that name. The minimal agent preset is also selectable under dsh sdk when a session is created.

dsh acp is kept with no options: it serves the Agent Client Protocol on stdio until the client disconnects, with the same launch form and exit statuses as dsh sdk. The protocol itself belongs to the SDK and ACP area.

Upstream forwards its arguments to pnpm in the profile directory because plugins are npm packages. Go plugins are local directories the operator placed, so the command becomes nested verbs (list, inspect, add, remove, grant, revoke, enable, disable) whose meaning the plugin area supplies; nothing is forwarded to a package manager and nothing is downloaded.

The note chooses how Node runs the launcher from TypeScript source (the tsx ESM hook, after Node 26 removed a flag). It exists only because of TypeScript and Node: a Go program is compiled, so there is no source launch, transform hook or path mapping to decide.

Read in full: every application process starts through dsh and one named profile, protocol profiles reserve standard output and route end of input and signals through bounded disposal, and no package may ship its own application binary. All of that is kept and is simpler with one Go binary. Changed: the profile is selected for programs with the explicit --profile form, and the entry-point scan the note enforces is unnecessary because the module has one main package.

Kept: a schema command that mounts nothing and also covers disabled entries. Dropped: the exit-1-when-partial rule and the widening rule, which exist because Schemastery validation mutates its input and evaluates JavaScript; a Go config type yields an exact JSON Schema and no plugin module is imported, so dsh config schema has no partial result to signal and exits by the common status table.

Kept as written: the command reference is generated from the real command tree and from each shipped profile's app, and a test fails when the committed file is stale. In Go it is the commands catalog (dsh catalog commands) rendered from the same Spec values the parser uses, so no help text is captured from a child process and no bilingual pairing is needed.

title: The config schema dump imports plugin modules, can block or keep handles open, and neither forces an exit nor cleans up
The start-up failure report dumps raw error objects and only warns that it may contain credential values
One fixed five-second limit forces every shutdown, cutting a turn and its final events

reason: Schemas are derived from compiled-in Go config types, so dsh config schema runs as a read-only admin command that starts no component and no plugin process; there is no imported code that could hang or hold a handle.

A secret is a redacting type in every text, JSON and log form, so an error chain cannot carry its value into a report; the report itself is the host area's bounded and pruned fatal diagnostic, and this area supplies the exit statuses and the commands that list and show it.

The stop function cancels running turns with a typed cause, waits for the agent teardown's bounded final flush, and only then applies a configurable exit deadline; when the deadline does pass the exit is reported as forced (status 124) and handled as a crash on resume.
